questions.solution:
Raymond's algorithm (distributed mutual exclusion) uses a single token passed along a tree. Since only the token holder enters the critical section and requests follow tree edges, no circular wait can form [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] no deadlock. With greedy token passing, a node may keep being bypassed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] starvation is possible.

Answer: no deadlock, but starvation may occur

options: no starvation, but deadlock may occur in rare cases
no deadlock, but starvation may occur
neither deadlock nor starvation can occur
deadlock may occur in cases where the process is already starved

questions.text: Consider a paging system that uses 1-level page table residing in main memory and a TLB for address translation. Each main memory access takes 100 ns and TLB lookup takes 20 ns. Each page transfer to/from the disk takes 5000 ns. Assume that the TLB hit ratio is 95%, page fault rate is 10%. Assume that for 20% of the total page faults, a dirty page has to be written back to disk before the required page is read from disk. TLB update time is negligible. The average memory access time in ns (round off to 1 decimal places) is ___________
questions.solution:
TLB lookup (20 ns) always happens.
- TLB hit (0.95): 1 memory access = 100 ns
- TLB miss (0.05): page table access 100 ns, then
[latex]\quad[/latex]no fault (0.9): 100 ns
[latex]\quad[/latex]fault (0.1): read page 5000 ns + dirty write-back (20%) 0.2 [latex]\times[/latex] 5000 + access 100 = 6100 ns

[latex]20+0.95(100)+0.05\,[100+0.9(100)+0.1(6100)]=20+95+0.05(800)=155[/latex] ns

Answer: 155

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
Consider the following set of processes, assumed to have arrived at time 0. Consider the CPU scheduling algorithms Shortest Job First (SJF) and Round Robin (RR). For RR, assume that the processes are scheduled in the order [latex]P_1,P_2,P_3,P_4[/latex].

If the time quantum for RR is 4 ms, then the absolute value of the difference between the average turnaround times (in ms) of SJF and RR (round off to 2 decimal places is_______
questions.solution:
SJF (P3 2, P4 4, P2 7, P1 8): completion 2, 6, 13, 21 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] average TAT = 42 / 4 = 10.5

RR, q = 4: P1 0-4, P2 4-8, P3 8-10 (done), P4 10-14 (done), P1 14-18 (done), P2 18-21 (done)
TAT: P1 18, P2 21, P3 10, P4 14 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] average = 63 / 4 = 15.75

|15.75 [latex]-[/latex] 10.5| = 5.25

Answer: 5.25

questions.text:
Consider the following five disk five disk access requests of the form (request id, cylinder number) that are present in the disk scheduler queue at a given time.

(P,155),(Q,85),(R,110),(S,30),(T,115)

Assume the head is positioned at cylinder 100. The scheduler follows Shortest Seek Time First scheduling to service the requests.

Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
questions.solution:
SSTF from 100:
R (110, distance 10) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T (115, 5) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q (85, 30) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S (30, 55) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P (155, 125)

- T before P True
- "Q after S but before T": Q is served before S and after T [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] FALSE
- Direction reverses between Q and P (down to S, then up to P) True
- R before P True

Answer: Q is serviced after S, but before T

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Q is serviced after S, but before T.
The head reverses its direction of movement between servicing of Q and P.
